title: Choose the BugReceipt landing structure
question: All three directions use the extension’s midnight, amber, and mint identity. Choose the clearest way to introduce BugReceipt, or re-roll the structures.

options.label: One Bug, Fully Traced
options.thesis: Follow one failed submission as BugReceipt turns it into a reviewable local report.
options.viewport: A minimal headline and Web Store action sit beside one continuous evidence trace that moves from the browser failure into the real extension review UI.
options.risk: The trace must stay sparse or the first viewport could feel more technical than inviting.

options.label: The 33-Second Failure
options.thesis: A compact timeline makes the product understandable as one deliberate capture-review-export sequence.
options.viewport: The page opens on a large 00:00–00:33 timeline with three decisive moments, a concise promise, the Web Store action, and an optional demo link.
options.risk: A timeline can resemble a decorative stepper unless the real extension evidence remains dominant.

options.label: The Evidence Receipt
options.thesis: The landing page behaves like the product: every feature visibly adds to one local evidence receipt.
options.viewport: A narrow receipt rail lists Screen, Console, Network, and Steps while a generous product stage explains the benefit and shows the extension at work.
options.risk: The receipt metaphor is closest to the app and therefore the least surprising direction.
